subject: Shiny : reactive variable with multiple dependencies

messages.author: 22e7e06bd1b3727b
messages.subject: Shiny : reactive variable with multiple dependencies
parts:
Hello,

Below I've included a server.r and ui.r file.  The design of the program is to generate a user-specificied number of entries (n()) from a population (also user specified) (N()).  The program should then highlight the selected tiles and display a list of the chosen tiles below.  Eventually, I hope to be able to contain a history of these entries (the samps variable is currently keeping track: on line 69 -- paste(c("Sample: ", sort(tail(samps, n())))) can be converted to paste(c("Sample: ",samps ))).

When this program is run, sometimes it seems that samps has an entry added to it and then is written to output, while at other times it seems that samps is written, and then an entry is appended.  Is there a way to force the appending to occur before the writing.  There might be some helpful code on 26-29, but I don't entirely understand its functionality.

Furthermore, in the ideal world, samps would be reset to an empty list when the user changes either or both of the sample size or the population size, so I set up an observe function at the end to try to do this.

Any help or pointers would be much appreciated!

#######################################
#######################################

SERVER.R

#######################################
#######################################

library("ggplot2")
library("shiny")

#runGitHub("shiny-examples", "rstudio", subdir = "012-datatables")
## predefining positions
#get.perm <- function(seed, pop.size) {
#  set.seed(seed)
#  sample(1:pop.size)
#}

ncols <- 10 #defaults to 10 columns in the display population
samps <<- c() # will hold the samples

shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
  
  ## define population
  #grab values
  N <- reactive(input$N)
  n <- reactive(input$n)
  #####
  #caculate number of rows/columns
  ncols.pop <- reactive(c(10,20,40,60)[(c(0,100,400,800) < N()) & (N() <= c(100,400,800,1000))])
  nrows.pop <- reactive(ceiling(N()/ncols.pop()))
  
  #set up the variable go to be in a position to keep track of dirty flags
  values <- reactiveValues(go = TRUE) 
  session$onFlushed(function() {
    values$go <- FALSE
  })
  
  #this will go and eventually draw our population
  grid.pop <- reactive({
    if (input$sample==0) { #if submit button has not been pressed
      return(data.frame(expand.grid(x=1:ncols.pop(),y=nrows.pop():1)[1:input$N,], 
                        label=1:input$N, sampled="FALSE"))
    }
    #if the button has been pressed
    samps <<- c(samps, sample(1:N(), n(), replace=FALSE))
    data.frame(expand.grid(x=1:ncols.pop(),y=nrows.pop():1)[1:N(),], label=1:N(), sampled=1:N() %in% tail(samps, n()))
  })
  
  ## output population plot
  output$popplot <- renderPlot({
    
    plot <- ggplot(grid.pop(),aes(x=x, y=y, label=label, fill=sampled)) + 
      geom_tile(color="black", size=1.3, alpha=0.8, show_guide=FALSE) +
      geom_text(size=5, show_guide=FALSE) +
      labs(title="Population") +
      theme_bw() +
      theme(text=element_text(size=24),
            panel.grid = element_blank(),
            panel.border = element_blank(),
            axis.text = element_blank(),
            axis.ticks = element_blank(),
            axis.title = element_blank()
      ) +
      scale_fill_manual(values=c("lightblue","lightgreen"))
    
    print(plot)
  })
  
  ##caption text
  output$sample <- renderText({
    if (values$go) #check for dirty flag 
      return(NULL)
    else{
      #don't display things that don't exist!
      if (input$sample == 0) return("Sample: ")
      paste(c("Sample: ", sort(tail(samps, n()))))
    }
  })
  
  observe({
    input$n
    input$N
    samps <<- c()
  })
})

#######################################
#######################################
#######################################
#######################################
#######################################

UI.R

#######################################
#######################################
#######################################
#######################################
#######################################

shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
    headerPanel("Random Sample"),
    sidebarPanel(
          wellPanel(
            helpText(""),
            numericInput("N", "Select Population Size", min=1, max=1000, value=20, step = 1)
            ),
          wellPanel(
            helpText(""),
            numericInput("n", "Select Sample Size", min=1, max=999, value=4, step = 1),
            actionButton("sample", "Sample", icon = icon("refresh"))
            )
        ),  #end sidebar panel


    mainPanel(
    plotOutput("popplot"),
    h4(textOutput("sample"))
        ) #end mainpanel
))
